items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: D.D. Chandler and Cantrell, the drummer and the drum, and the maker, it sounded like it would turn a piece of cloth.

ctx.x: Did he play a lot of roles, or would he play like what? Huh? Did he play a lot of drum rolls, or what style did he play?

Yeah, he played a lot of roles and everything. D.D. Chandler and Cantrell, the drummer and the drum, and the maker, it sounded like it would turn a piece of cloth. Well, see, those fellas used sharp drums. All good. Tuned it up high, you mean, had it up tight or what?

items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1962-04-11
items.q: I used to second line and watched them play. And I said I always did want to play like them men. And I used to see me walk, I walked in like 3D Chandler.

ctx.x: And then, him too. Them was two men. Boy, they used to look for all these people. Boy, them drummers would talk with J.D. would be so drunk. Drunk he didn't know what they did. But they could play it out. They played drunk with so. Sometimes they'd go get him out of the way. He'd be drunk. And I just watched them two tell us. Them two men when I was young, I used to second line and watched them play. And I said I always did want to play like them men. And I used to see me walk, I walked in like 3D Chandler. Fly,…
that band. I have, but I don't know much about it. No, it's been so long. I can't say much
